lead: 14 public holidays, including national, regional and local days. The complete calendar of non-working days in the city of Valencia for 2026, with the traditions and celebrations of each date.

In 2026, Valencia enjoys 14 official public holidays: 8 national ones common to all of Spain, 4 regional ones specific to the Comunitat Valenciana and 2 local holidays exclusive to the city of Valencia — San Vicente Mártir (22 January) and San Vicente Ferrer (28 April). The year is marked by two especially generous long weekends: Easter (Good Friday + Easter Monday = 4 days) and early October (9 d’Octubre + 12 October on a Monday).
Dates, type of holiday and the cultural tradition associated with each day off in Valencia.

items.title: January
facts: 1 Jan
Thursday · New Year’s Day · national · Start of the year. The Plaza del Ayuntamiento hosts the New Year’s Eve chimes and the first events of the year.
6 Jan
Tuesday · Epiphany of the Lord · Three Kings · national · Three Kings Parade through the centre of Valencia on the eve. The excitement of the little ones on the most magical night of winter.
22 Jan

Thursday · San Vicente Mártir · local · Local holiday exclusive to the city of Valencia. Patron saint of the city, a Valencian martyr of the 4th century. Celebrated with religious events and the re-enactment of the baptism of San Vicente Ferrer.

items.title: March
facts: 19 Mar

Thursday · San José · Las Fallas · national · The most eagerly awaited night of the year. The “cremà” burns all the fallas in a spectacular display of fire and pyrotechnics. The big day of Valencia’s greatest festival, Intangible Heritage of Humanity.

items.title: April
facts: 3 Apr

Friday · Good Friday · national · Semana Santa Marinera in the Poblados Marítimos, with unique processions of brotherhoods of grenadiers in Napoleonic style. One of the most singular Holy Weeks in Spain.
6 Apr
Monday · Easter Monday · regional · Regional holiday of the Comunitat Valenciana. Together with Good Friday, it creates a four-day long weekend at Easter.
28 Apr

Tuesday · San Vicente Ferrer · local · Local holiday of the city of Valencia and patron saint of the Comunitat Valenciana. The “miracles” of San Vicente are staged, street plays that re-enact miracles of the saint in squares and neighbourhoods.

items.title: May
facts: 1 May
Friday · Labour Day · national · National holiday. In Valencia it coincides with the approach of the feast of the Virgen de los Desamparados, patron saint of the city.
10 May

Sunday · Virgen de los Desamparados · reference · Patron saint of Valencia and the Comunitat. On the second Sunday of May, the Plaza de la Virgen fills with flowers and dances. The transfer of the image from the Basilica to the Cathedral is one of the most moving moments of the year.

items.title: June
facts: 24 Jun

Wednesday · Fogueres de Sant Joan · regional · Regional holiday of the Comunitat Valenciana. The Saint John bonfires fill Valencia’s beaches on the shortest night of the year. A millennia-old tradition that celebrates the summer solstice with fire and gunpowder.

items.title: August
facts: 15 Aug
Saturday · Assumption of the Virgin · national · National holiday in the height of summer. Valencia enjoys its peak tourist activity and the summer festivals are at their height.

items.title: October
facts: 9 Oct

Friday · Day of the Comunitat Valenciana · regional · The great Valencian holiday. It commemorates the entry of King Jaume I into Valencia in 1238. The Senyera parades in a civic procession from the City Hall to the Parterre. Moors and Christians parade and regional dances.
12 Oct
Monday · National Day of Spain · national · Hispanic Day. In 2026 it falls on a Monday, creating a long weekend together with 9 October.

items.title: November
facts: 1 Nov
Sunday · All Saints’ Day · national · A day of reflection and tribute to the departed. Valencia’s cemeteries receive thousands of visitors with flowers.
2 Nov
Monday · All Souls’ Day · regional · Regional holiday of the Comunitat Valenciana, recoverable. Complements All Saints’ Day.

items.title: December
facts: 6 Dec
Sunday · Spanish Constitution Day · national · Commemoration of the Constitution of 1978. National holiday.
8 Dec
Tuesday · Immaculate Conception · national · Religious feast. In Valencia the Christmas atmosphere is already felt, with the switching on of the lights and the first nativity scenes.
25 Dec

Friday · Christmas Day · national · The great family festival of winter. Valencia celebrates Christmas with artistic nativity scenes, the Expojove fair and the unique atmosphere of the illuminated Plaza del Ayuntamiento.

blocks.title: Notable long weekends of 2026 in Valencia
items: Easter (3–6 Apr): Good Friday + Easter Monday = 4 consecutive days off
San Vicente Ferrer (25–28 Apr): Local holiday on Tuesday, possible long weekend bridge
October (9–13 Oct): 9 d’Octubre (Friday) + 12 October (Monday) = double long weekend
Christmas (25–27 Dec): Christmas on a Friday creates a natural three-day break through to Sunday
San José / Fallas (19 Mar): Falls on a Thursday → possible 4-day Fallas bridge
Immaculate Conception (8 Dec): Falls on a Tuesday → possible bridge with the previous weekend
